# Results — Study 767 (VIX9D-Term) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The short-end VIX
term-structure slope (log(^VIX / ^VIX9D)) is tested as a predictor of SPY forward
returns and as a binary timing overlay.  Contango (slope > 0, ^VIX9D < ^VIX, the
normal upward front end) is the claimed 'risk-on' state; backwardation (slope < 0,
^VIX9D above ^VIX) is the claimed near-term stress signal.  Real daily tape: ^VIX9D,
^VIX, SPY from 2011-01-04 (^VIX9D history start) through 2026-07-10.  As-of
**2026-07-12**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | N days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| ^VIX9D, ^VIX, SPY | 2011-01-04 → 2026-07-10 | 3 901 | `5953babc50d3` |

Fraction of days in contango (slope > 0): **73.1%** — the front end spends most of its
time upward-sloping, but it inverts far more often than the ^VIX/^VIX3M curve (Study 111
sat in contango ~90% of the time). The 9-day tenor is the twitchiest point on the whole
volatility surface, so the near-term slope flips on any headline.

## The central test — Q5-Q1 quintile spread

Slope is sorted into rolling quintiles (252-day lookback, out-of-sample); forward SPY
log-returns are computed for each bucket; the Q5 (steepest contango) minus Q1 (deepest
backwardation) spread is the decisive test of the claim.

| Horizon | n Q5 | n Q1 | mean Q5 (bps) | mean Q1 (bps) | spread (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 day** | 874 | 784 | **+5.94** | **+8.73** | **−2.79** | **−0.35** |
| **5 days** | 871 | 784 | +21.73 | +31.98 | −10.25 | −0.36 |
| **21 days** | 869 | 778 | +83.47 | +151.33 | −67.86 | −1.10 |

The Q5-Q1 spread is **negative at all horizons** — the opposite of the claim.
Backwardation episodes (Q1, near-term stress, front-end inversion) are followed by
*better* average SPY returns than the calmest contango days (Q5).  Every HAC t-stat is
well inside ±2 and points in the wrong direction.

### Full quintile forward-return table (h = 1 day)

| Quintile | Regime | n | mean (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Q1 | Deepest backwardation | 784 | +8.73 | +1.65 |
| Q2 | Mild backwardation | 697 | +5.16 | +1.33 |
| Q3 | Near-flat / transition | 725 | +2.68 | +0.79 |
| Q4 | Moderate contango | 758 | +3.25 | +1.17 |
| Q5 | Steepest contango | 874 | +5.94 | +2.80 |

The pattern is **U-shaped, not monotone**: the extremes (deep backwardation Q1 and
steep contango Q5) both earn more than the flat middle (Q3). There is no ascending
staircase from backwardation to contango — the single feature the claim predicts.

## Binary timing overlay — long in contango, flat in backwardation

The 'risk-on' rule: be long SPY when yesterday's slope was positive, else hold cash.

| Arm | mean (bps/day) | Ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Timing overlay (active)** | **+3.64** | **+0.83** | **+3.41** |
| **Buy-and-hold (passive)** | **+5.27** | **+0.78** | **+3.42** |
| **Spread (active − passive)** | **−1.64** | — | **−1.45** |

The timer *underperforms* buy-and-hold by **1.64 bps/day** (~−4.1%/yr) at zero cost.
The spread t-stat is −1.45 — not conventionally significant, but consistently on the
wrong side. Because the front end is in backwardation ~27% of the time, the timer sits
in cash roughly one day in four — including some of the highest-returning post-shock
reversals.

### Cost sweep (spread = active − passive)

~**37 switches per year** (contango↔backwardation transitions) — the twitchy 9-day
tenor flips regime nearly three times as often as the ^VIX/^VIX3M curve, so friction
bites hard.

| Round-trip cost | Spread (bps/day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps | −1.64 | −1.45 |
| 0.5 bps | −1.71 | −1.51 |
| 1.0 bps | −1.78 | −1.58 |
| 2.0 bps | −1.93 | −1.70 |
| 5.0 bps | −2.37 | −2.09 |

The spread starts negative and only deteriorates with costs — **there is no positive
break-even cost**, and by 5 bps/switch the underperformance is itself *significant*
(*t* = −2.09).

## Regime comparison — the key finding

| Regime | n | % of tape | mean (bps/day) | Ann. Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Full sample | 3 899 | 100% | +5.26 | +0.77 | +3.41 |
| **Contango (slope > 0)** | 2 851 | 73.1% | **+4.97** | **+0.97** | **+3.48** |
| **Backwardation (slope < 0)** | 1 048 | 26.9% | **+6.04** | **+0.60** | **+1.43** |

Here is the honest subtlety of this study. On a **risk-adjusted** basis contango *does*
look better — Sharpe 0.97 vs 0.60 — because backwardation days are far more volatile.
But the timer does not harvest Sharpe; it harvests **raw return**, and backwardation
days average **+6.04 bps/day vs +4.97** in contango. The 'stress' regime delivers *more*
raw return, not less. So the slope really does carry information — about **volatility** —
but pointing it at **direction** gets you the wrong answer: you flee the more volatile
days, which are also the higher-returning ones (the classic volatility-risk-premium
rebound).

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Q5-Q1 spread is −2.79 bps (wrong sign) with HAC *t* = −0.35
  at h = 1d. No horizon produces a t-stat above 0 in the predicted direction; the
  quintile pattern is U-shaped, not monotone. The ^VIX9D/^VIX slope does not predict
  SPY forward returns.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The timing overlay trails buy-and-hold by ~4.1%/yr at zero
  cost; ~37 switches/yr mean every bp of switching cost widens the gap, and by 5 bps the
  underperformance is significant. No positive break-even cost exists.
- **Beats buy-and-hold? — NO.** The timer sits flat during backwardation, the
  higher-*raw*-return regime (+6.04 vs +4.97 bps/day), missing the strongest post-shock
  rebounds. The slope predicts vol, not direction.
